per_run.approach_summary: Explored all 106 anonymized features, their cardinalities, marginal associations, class balance, duplicate patterns, and target stability over row-order deciles. The target was rare (3.36%). Signal was concentrated in several low-cardinality feature blocks but all-feature models substantially beat restricted-block models, indicating useful distributed signal and interactions. Compared regularized logistic regression, LightGBM, Extra Trees, and CatBoost using 5-fold stratified and forward (first 3500 to last 1500) validation. Full-feature CatBoost was strongest on forward validation (about 0.826 AUC); confirmation AUCs were 0.7821 LightGBM, 0.8036 Extra Trees, and 0.8324 CatBoost. Shallower, deeper, and longer CatBoost variants scored 0.8181-0.8195, so they were rejected. Rank blends of the primary CatBoost and Extra Trees improved confirmation performance: weights of 0.70 and 0.75 on CatBoost both reached 0.8348, versus 0.8344 at 0.80 and 0.8341 at 0.85/0.90. Final predictions use the midpoint, 0.725 CatBoost plus 0.275 Extra Trees, blended by within-split ranks for calibration robustness.

Explored all 106 anonymized features, missingness, univariate signal, duplicates, class balance, and target/drift behavior across row-order blocks. Compared standardized logistic regression, Extra Trees, LightGBM, random forest, and CatBoost using five-fold stratified CV plus a forward holdout chosen because confirmation/transfer row IDs form later contiguous blocks. Nonlinear tree models clearly dominated: Extra Trees scored 0.796 shuffled CV and 0.851 forward-holdout AUC; LightGBM was complementary. Confirmation feedback supported this pattern (logistic 0.7017, LightGBM 0.7623, Extra Trees 0.8109). Tests over leaf sizes and feature fractions showed leaf sizes 2-3 and high feature fractions were strongest; RF and CatBoost were weaker alone. Probability and rank blends were then tested. The selected final rank ensemble combines 50% baseline Extra Trees (leaf 3), 25% independent Extra Trees (leaf 2), 15% LightGBM, and 10% CatBoost; it achieved the best confirmation AUC, 0.8135, versus 0.8113 for the best probability blend and 0.8128 for a two-Extra-Trees rank blend. All component models were trained on all research rows.

Profiled all 106 anonymized features, including missingness, cardinality, univariate AUC, target prevalence across ordered row blocks, and the consecutive research/confirmation/transfer row windows. Used five-fold stratified out-of-fold AUC to compare standardized logistic regression, random forests, histogram boosting, LightGBM, CatBoost, and ExtraTrees variants with different leaf smoothing and feature subsampling. Linear modeling was weak (confirmation AUC 0.7017); tree methods captured substantial nonlinear interaction signal. The strongest single model was ExtraTrees with min_samples_leaf=2 and broad feature sampling (confirmation AUC 0.8206); fully grown ExtraTrees and CatBoost scored 0.8145 and 0.8183. Boosted and heavily smoothed alternatives were useful mainly for diversity. Tested rank-averaged ensembles to reduce calibration sensitivity across the ordered data windows. Confirmation feedback improved the ensemble from 0.8307-0.8348 to 0.8371. Final transfer predictions use a rank blend of 45% leaf-2 ExtraTrees, 45% CatBoost, and 10% fully grown ExtraTrees, with each component refit on all 5,000 labeled research rows.

Loaded all 106 anonymized features and profiled cardinality, missingness, marginal AUC, duplicate overlap, row-order prevalence, and block-to-block distribution shift. Compared stratified 5-fold and last-1000 chronological validation for regularized LightGBM models, Extra Trees, random forest, and logistic regression, both on all features and on feature-family ablations. The target was rare (3.36%). Internal random/chronological AUCs included 0.778/0.808 for all-feature LightGBM, 0.781/0.828 for features 0-80, 0.763/0.801 for features 0-14, 0.787/0.850 for all-feature Extra Trees, and only 0.644/0.693 for features 81-105 alone. Nineteen confirmation calls were made. Representative confirmation AUCs were: all-feature LightGBM 0.7775, shallower all-feature LightGBM 0.7849, Extra Trees 0.8018, logistic 0.6938, late-family-only 0.6784, and first-15-feature LightGBM 0.8310. Capacity variants and alternate model families on the first block scored 0.7899-0.8304; removing feature 14 or features 13-14 scored 0.8240, showing the result was not a single-feature accident but that the full block helped. The final predictor is an 80/20 rank blend of the five-fold first-15 model and the five-fold features-0-80 model; confirmation AUC was 0.8314, narrowly above the first-block model. I attacked the best confirmation result as potentially confirmation-specific: checked exact overlaps, feature ablations, model-family dependence, temporal holdout, distribution shifts, and blends with broader models. Only 24 confirmation and 30 transfer rows exactly matched research feature vectors, and all matched research groups for those rows were negative, so overlap cannot explain the overall AUC; exact transfer matches use their observed research group mean. The transfer feature distributions were closer to research than confirmation in every broad family, and the broader 0-80 model was stronger in both random and chronological validation. Thus confirmation does favor the compact block under drift, but the evidence did not invalidate it; retaining 20% of the broader model hedges against the transfer shift while preserving the strongest confirmed signal.

Explored all 106 anonymized features, including cardinality, missingness, univariate AUC, distribution drift, duplicates, and target prevalence over row-id blocks. Five-fold shuffled CV gave AUC 0.716 for regularized logistic regression, 0.790 for Extra Trees, 0.775 for CatBoost, and 0.801 for Random Forest, supporting nonlinear threshold/interaction structure. Local confirmation scores were 0.7003, 0.8056, 0.7908, and 0.8009 respectively; a CatBoost/Extra-Trees blend did not beat Extra Trees. I varied Extra-Trees leaf size and feature subsampling: the best all-feature variant scored 0.8130. I then attacked this result as potentially exploiting confirmation-specific drift and random-fold artifacts. I compared a contiguous last-1500-row research holdout, inspected importances, removed two conspicuously drifted feature blocks (indices 17-55 and 81-101), and tested narrower controls. The reduced stable/core set retained a 0.779 temporal-holdout AUC versus 0.776 for all features and improved confirmation to 0.8189; an early-only control fell to 0.7469, while a broader no-drift control scored 0.8109. Thus the attack found credible spurious/drift sensitivity and I revised the final approach. The final prediction is a 75/25 blend of five-fold Extra Trees on the stable/core set with minimum leaf sizes 1 and 3; this scored 0.8234 on confirmation, better than either component (0.8189 and 0.8176).

Loaded all 106 anonymized features and profiled missingness, cardinality, univariate associations, and class balance (168/5000 positives). Tested 5-fold cross-validated logistic regression, ExtraTrees, LightGBM, and CatBoost: AUCs were 0.7343, 0.7882, 0.7541, and 0.7769; their confirmation AUCs were 0.6984, 0.8065, 0.7539, and 0.8032. Regularization and feature-subset experiments showed that ExtraTrees with a supervised 40-feature subset captured useful multivariate interactions: cross-validated AUC 0.8023 and confirmation AUC 0.8193, versus 0.8061-0.8081 for full-feature/tree variants. Rank blends reached 0.8183 or less. I then attacked the best approach as potentially confirmation-specific. Research-vs-confirmation, research-vs-transfer, and confirmation-vs-transfer cohort classifiers had AUC 0.5086, 0.4875, and 0.5169; maximum marginal KS shifts were 0.037-0.042. Honest repeated holdouts with feature selection performed only inside each training split averaged 0.7801 (rare positives caused SD 0.0462), top-40 sets overlapped by 35.4/40 on average, and row_id-blocked validation averaged 0.7961. Thus selection leakage, row-order artifacts, and cohort drift were not convincing explanations. I also found a small number of exact repeated feature vectors; labeled repeats were consistently negative. A conservative exact-match override improved the selected model from 0.8193 to 0.8219 on confirmation (seed ensembles scored 0.8145, or 0.8170 with the override), supporting rather than undermining this rule. Final transfer predictions use the 40-feature ExtraTrees model plus that exact-match override.

DATA / STRUCTURE FINDINGS
The 106 anonymized columns are not a flat feature soup; they fall into three blocks with a
clear internal grammar. Block C0 (x_000-x_015) is a set of heavily zero-inflated counts.
Blocks A (x_016-x_053) and B (x_054-x_101) are near-mirror images of each other: pairing
columns by cross-block correlation lines up 17 pairs at r > 0.9 that also share exact upper
bounds (x_042/x_081 both max at 71737, x_048/x_091 at 70571, x_045/x_084/x_086 at 1834.75,
x_017/x_097 at ~670), so A and B measure the same underlying quantities under two different
views/windows. The last four columns behave like codes rather than magnitudes (x_102 with
1572 levels and ~68% level overlap into the held-out splits; x_103 375 levels; x_104/x_105
~37 levels each, with x_104==185 carrying a 10.6% positive rate against a 3.4% base).
Target prevalence is 168/5000 = 3.4%, which turned out to be the binding constraint on
everything below.

The most interesting finding was a subpopulation split, not a feature. Conditioning on
x_077>0 (23% of rows, 7.5% positive vs 2.1% elsewhere; x_104==185 is a near-duplicate
marker of the same group, 93% co-occurrence) the predictive feature set changes almost
completely. Inside that group the C0 block dominates -- x_000 reaches univariate AUC 0.778
and x_006 0.721, versus 0.606 and 0.612 pooled. Outside it, C0 is inert and the A/B cost
columns (x_044, x_083, x_055, x_099) carry the signal. The two regimes also differ in
level, not just in slope: mean x_000 is 59 vs 9 and mean x_015 is 38 vs 142 across the
split, consistent with two record types pooled into one table.

WHAT I DID, AND WHAT THE STRUCTURE WAS WORTH
I built a repeated 5-fold CV harness (5-8 seeds, seed-averaged rank OOF) because single-seed
CV on 168 positives moves +/-0.008 on noise alone, which is larger than most of the effects
I was testing. Adversarial validation gave AUC 0.50 for research-vs-confirmation and
0.50 for research-vs-transfer, so the splits are IID and CV is an unbiased guide.

The decisive lever was model capacity, not representation. Default-depth LightGBM scored
0.7705; forcing depth 2-3 with feature_fraction 0.3-0.5 and reg_lambda 5 jumped to
0.795-0.797, and strongly-regularized logistic regression on rank-gauss features reached
0.783 (C=0.001, monotone in regularization strength). Seed-bagging added a further ~0.006.

Almost everything I built from the structural findings failed to add anything, which I
consider the substantive result rather than a footnote:
- A/B pair ratios and differences, block-level nonzero counts, log-sum cost aggregates, and
  per-unit normalisations: 0.7947-0.8020 seedbag vs 0.8018 for raw features. Nothing.
- Explicit regime interaction terms (C0 features multiplied by the x_077>0 indicator):
  0.8033 vs 0.8018, inside noise. The depth-3 trees already represent the interaction.
- Training separate models per regime: 0.7874, clearly worse. Splitting 168 positives in
  two costs more than the regime-specific fits gain.
- Nested out-of-fold target encoding of x_102/x_103/x_104/x_105: 0.8009-0.8027 vs 0.8018.
  The high-cardinality codes carry no group-level target signal; consistently, their LightGBM
  gain importance sits *below* their permuted-target null importance.
- Feature selection looked like a +0.005 win (top-40 by importance, 0.8015 vs 0.7964) until
  I redid the selection inside each CV fold, at which point it returned 0.7960 -- the entire
  gain had been selection leakage. I dropped it.
- CatBoost (0.783), ExtraTrees (0.765), MLP (0.734-0.759), Gaussian NB (0.681), LightGBM
  extra_trees/GOSS/DART variants: none beat the tuned shallow LightGBM.
- Negative-undersampling bagged LightGBM (all positives + 10x negatives, 10 bags) matched
  the best single model at 0.8077 and was worth keeping for blend diversity.

FINAL MODEL
Equal-weight rank average of five families -- LightGBM depth 3, LightGBM depth 4, L2
logistic on rank-gauss features (C=0.001), RandomForest, and the undersampling-bagged
LightGBM -- each averaged over 8 seeds x 5 folds, and additionally averaged with the same
five families refit on 100% of the research rows. Seed-averaged OOF AUC 0.8092.

WHAT THE CONFIRMATION SCORES TOLD ME
Five calls. (1) 0.7933 for a single seed-bagged LightGBM plus 20% logistic (OOF 0.8057).
(2) 0.8050 for the first four-family blend (OOF 0.8044) -- confirming that cross-family
blending, not further tuning, was where the remaining gain was. (3) 0.8015 for the 8-seed
five-family blend (OOF 0.8092) and (4) 0.8016 for the identical blend refit on all research
rows -- an A/B that told me fold-averaged and full-data-fit predictions are interchangeable
here, so I averaged them. (5) 0.8015 for the exact submitted artifact.

The main thing confirmation taught me was where its own resolution ends. With ~50 positives
in 1500 rows a confirmation AUC carries roughly +/-0.025 of noise, so calls 2 and 3 differ
by less than the measurement error even though their OOF estimates differ by 0.005 in the
opposite direction. After call 3 I stopped using confirmation to rank candidates and used it
only to sanity-check the final artifact, deferring to the 5000-row seed-averaged OOF for
every model decision. I deliberately did not spend the remaining 15 calls hill-climbing a
1500-row proxy.

HONEST ASSESSMENT
The performance ceiling here is set by 168 positives, not by feature representation. The A/B
mirror-block structure and the x_077 regime split are real and reproducible descriptions of
how this table is built, and they explain why shallow depth-2/3 trees beat both deep trees
and purely additive models -- the signal needs interactions, but only a couple of levels of
them. They did not, however, convert into predictive gain, because the pooled shallow GBM
already extracts what they encode and every explicit encoding I tried spent degrees of
freedom the positive count could not fund.

DATA STRUCTURE FOUND (anonymised, but the schema is unambiguous)
5000 labelled rows, 3.36% positive (168), 106 features, 1500 confirmation + 1500 transfer rows.
Adversarial validation gave AUC 0.50/0.50/0.51 for research-vs-confirmation, research-vs-transfer and
confirmation-vs-transfer, so the three regions are an IID partition with no covariate shift.

Reverse-engineering the columns turned out to be the whole game. Two structural facts:

(1) The continuous columns are MONETARY AMOUNTS and the integer columns are COUNTS, and they come in
    exact (sum, count) pairs. For 28 pairs -- e.g. (x_047,x_016), (x_048,x_017), (x_042,x_097),
    (x_081,x_054), (x_090,x_064) -- the zero patterns agree on 100.0% of all 8000 rows, and
    sum/count lands in a plausible per-transaction amount range. x_015 is the CURRENT amount
    (median 67.95; 48.5% non-integer; values like 57.95 / 209.95 / 7.4041). x_080 is constant.
    x_102-x_105 are offset-encoded categoricals (x_104 is essentially binary: value 185 -> 10.6%
    positive vs value 150 -> 2.5%). x_014 is a time-delta.

(2) The first 14 columns (x_000..x_013) are a COMPOSITION -- counts of the same activity broken out by
    type. The target depends on the MIX, not the level. Pairwise count ratios are far stronger than
    any raw column: best raw feature AUC 0.681, but (x_000+1)/(x_005+1) alone gives AUC 0.738, and
    the product of two such ratios reaches 0.769 -- from two features. A plain logistic regression on
    the 14 centred-log-ratio (CLR) coordinates of that block alone gives CV AUC 0.765. x_004/x_005/
    x_009/x_012/x_013 sit in the denominator (protective), x_000/x_001/x_002/x_006/x_008/x_011 in
    the numerator. Trees cannot form a ratio, so a model reading the raw counts has to approximate a
    2-D ray boundary with axis-aligned splits, which is exactly the structure a generic model misses.

WHAT I BUILT
Feature set = 106 raw columns + three engineered families:
  * cr_* : 78 pairwise count ratios (x_i+1)/(x_j+1) within the 14-count composition, plus within-row
           shares of each count in the row total (the compositional view).
  * rel_*: current amount / historical mean amount for each of the 28 (sum,count) pairs, i.e.
           x_015 / (sum_w / count_w) -- "is this purchase unusual for this account's own history".
           Also a prior-excluding variant (sum-cur)/(count-1) and cross-window dispersion.
  * ra_/rb_ count ratios inside the two smaller count families, amount decimal-count (3-decimal
    amounts -> 9.6% positive vs 3.6% base, the classic FX-conversion tell), cents pattern.
Model = LightGBM, deliberately tiny (num_leaves 2-8, lr 0.01-0.015, colsample 0.15-0.5, 900-2500
trees, subsample 0.7, reg_lambda 10), 6 configurations x 5 seeds x 10 stratified folds, rank-averaged
(300 fits). With only 168 positives, capacity is the binding constraint: num_leaves=31 scored 0.790,
num_leaves=4 scored 0.821. Hyperparameters are otherwise flat (all 27 grid points 0.815-0.819), so I
averaged six configurations rather than picking one after looking at the numbers.

ABLATIONS (repeated stratified CV on research rows)
  raw 106 columns                     0.795
  count ratios cr_* alone (78 feats)  0.791   <- 14 raw columns, re-expressed as ratios, match all 106
  cr_* + shares                       0.791
  cr_* + shares + rel_*               0.818
  full engineered set, 10-fold        0.826
Things that did NOT help and were dropped or left in only as noise: target encoding of the four
categoricals (nested, several smoothings: 0.819-0.821 vs 0.821 without); CLR coordinates added to the
GBM (0.819); amount log-ratios across windows (0.820); CatBoost (0.796), RandomForest (0.800),
ExtraTrees (0.795), logistic regression (0.762-0.785); dart/goss boosting; negative-downsampling bags;
blending any of these with the GBM (best blend 0.8256 vs 0.8252 alone -- noise).

CONFIRMATION SCORING (6 calls)
  1. raw-features baseline, same model class        CV 0.795 -> confirmation 0.7905
  2. engineered set, 5 seeds x 5 folds              CV 0.821 -> confirmation 0.8239
  3. engineered set, 10 seeds x 5 folds             CV 0.825 -> confirmation 0.8240
  4. same, pool-derived features removed            CV 0.822 -> confirmation 0.8351
  5. 6-config ensemble, no pool features, 5-fold    CV 0.822 -> confirmation 0.8354
  6. 6-config ensemble, no pool features, 10-fold   CV 0.826 -> confirmation 0.8350   <- SUBMITTED
Calls 1-2 are the load-bearing ones: they confirm out-of-sample that the +0.03 from feature
engineering is real and not a CV artifact. Calls 4-6 differ by 0.0004 from each other, i.e. the final
number is stable across fold counts, seeds and hyperparameter configurations.

ATTACKING MY OWN APPROACH
I tried five specific ways for the confirmation score to be misleading. One of them succeeded, before
any confirmation call, and changed the model:

(a) LEAKY FEATURE SELECTION -- FOUND, FIXED. Ranking features by importance on the full research set
    and keeping the top 40 "improved" CV to 0.8251. Redoing the selection strictly inside each training
    fold collapsed it to 0.8078 (top-60 0.8136, top-100 0.8159) -- all WORSE than using every feature
    (0.821). The apparent gain was pure selection leakage. I use the full feature set; no selection.

(b) TRANSDUCTIVE / POOL FEATURES -- FOUND, REMOVED. Frequency encodings over the pooled 8000 unlabelled
    rows and x_102 group statistics ranked #1 and #3 by gain importance, which looked like the score
    might be resting on pool-composition artifacts. Ablating them changed CV by less than the seed
    noise (0.8178 vs 0.8173 at 3 seeds, 0.8215 vs 0.8245 at 10 seeds -- inconsistent in sign), so they
    carry no real signal, and they make predictions depend on the exact unlabelled pool. Dropped on
    parsimony grounds; confirmation independently preferred the smaller set (0.8351 vs 0.8240), though
    that 0.011 gap is inside the ~0.03 standard error of a 1500-row / ~50-positive AUC and I do not
    claim it is real.

(c) ENTITY LEAKAGE VIA x_102 -- QUANTIFIED, NOT DISQUALIFYING. x_102 is a repeating entity id (2102
    distinct values over 8000 rows, groups up to 134 rows); 81.5% of confirmation rows and 78.5% of
    transfer rows share an x_102 value with some research row, and the within-group positive-pair rate
    is 0.00133 vs 0.00113 expected under independence. Grouped CV that never puts an entity in both
    train and validation scores 0.809 vs 0.817 for random CV, so about 0.008 AUC is entity-level
    memorisation. Crucially the entity overlap is nearly identical for confirmation and transfer, so
    this inflates both equally and does not make the confirmation score a misleading proxy for
    transfer. It does mean ~0.008 of the headline number is not "understanding the phenomenon".

(d) COINCIDENTAL ROW OVERLAP -- REFUTED. 24/1500 confirmation rows and 30/1500 transfer rows are exact
    feature-vector duplicates of a research row; transfer overlaps MORE, and duplicated rows receive
    below-average predicted scores (mean rank 611 vs 753 for confirmation), so they cannot be carrying
    the score. Nearest-neighbour distances into research are essentially the same for confirmation and
    transfer (median 1.91 vs 1.69; zero exact-distance matches after quantile standardisation), and the
    fraction of feature values never seen in research is 0.0239 for confirmation vs 0.0247 for transfer.

(e) SPURIOUS DRIVING FEATURE -- REFUTED. The count-ratio story survives being attacked directly: the
    univariate AUC of (x_000+1)/(x_005+1) has a 200-sample bootstrap 95% interval of [0.693, 0.785],
    and after trimming the extreme 4% of its range it still scores 0.689 on the middle mass, so it is
    not a handful of outliers. The rel_* amount-vs-history block was tested with 10 repeated honest
    50/50 splits (fit on half, score the untouched half): +0.0235 AUC, paired s.d. 0.0115, winning
    9 of 10 repeats. row_id carries no signal (AUC 0.4998) and target rate is flat across row_id
    deciles, so there is no ordering artifact.

Residual risk I am NOT able to rule out: confirmation-set adaptation. I made 6 scoring calls and
exactly one binary choice (b) was informed by them, on a difference I have argued is noise; if that
choice is wrong the cost is ~0.01 AUC. And the transfer grading may weight or subset rows differently
than the plain AUC the local tool returns, which no amount of local analysis can detect.

Expected transfer AUC: ~0.82-0.84, i.e. matching confirmation, since the two regions are
statistically indistinguishable in covariates, novelty and predicted-score distribution
(Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic 0.010, p = 1.00, between the confirmation and transfer prediction
distributions).
